t: You're on Dean Farrar Street, in the City of Westminster. It is named after Frederic Farrar, a senior Church of England clergyman who was also a philologist, an author and a schoolteacher. He was a pallbearer at Charles Darwin's funeral in 1882, and he belonged to the Cambridge Apostles, a secret society. Farrar served as Archdeacon of Westminster from 1883 to 1894. In 1895 he became Dean of Canterbury, and he held that post until he died in 1903. The street keeps his title and his name.
